The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed for shoppers
Why, in plain words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary made the account page fail with a division by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought before but not yet this month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 7m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 4,486.73 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #570 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed for shoppers while monthly-spend-feature was on
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 10:10 to 10:17 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 5 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 10:20:31 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 10:16:02 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 10:10 UTC and was back to normal at 10:17 UTC, 7 minutes later. 28.9% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.9% before it began. At its worst, 40.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 4,486.73 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching on a new monthly spending summary made the account page fail with a division by zero, likely for shoppers who had bought before but not yet this month. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #570, for a person to review and merge. Switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could make account pages fail again in the same way.

Impact
7m 0s - onset until back to normal
40.5% - peak error rate
2,424 - requests failed
0.9% to 28.9% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
4,486.73 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month` and does not handle an empty list. So for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns that error into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 10:10–10:16
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 occurrences in 37 minutes, 09:40–10:16; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 10:13
why 1 Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 during 10:10–10:16 UTC. No such error was logged before then.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 36 occurrences in 30 minutes, 09:40–10:09
why 2 The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at 10:10:31 UTC. Before that it was evaluated off and account pages rendered normally. Evaluations were split between off and on at 10:10 UTC and were all on during 10:11–10:16 UTC.
  Evidence:
    P1 10:10:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 09:40–10:09
    Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 occurrences in 26 minutes, 09:41–10:06
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 10:10
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 10:11–10:16
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 10:11; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change.
      T7
      T8
    Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read.
      T14 10:16:12 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 10:16:12
why 3 With the flag on, account page requests reached a monthly per-item spend calculation that divides by zero for shoppers with no purchases this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- The flag change reached all account page traffic almost at once: evaluations were split briefly and then all on. No staged rollout or health check that would hold back or undo a flag change was seen. (AI-3)
- No test of the flag-on path for a shopper with past purchases but none this month was seen before the flag was switched on. Code-Fix says the cases it adds would raise against the current code. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 10:10:31 UTC. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% to 20-40%. | 0.93 | confirmed

Trigger
monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 10:10:31 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 10:16:13 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 10:19:03 | Proposed a fix: PR #570 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 10:10 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 10:16 UTC, 6 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #570 | open
AI-3 | Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop in stages, with an error-rate check that stops the rollout and turns the flag back off when errors rise. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Require tests that exercise a flag's on path to pass in CI before that flag can be switched on in production. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 12 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 13 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 2 minutes 9 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 3 minutes 3 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #570.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 12 10:10 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began
 | 10:16 | DETECTED | HighErrorRate on io-shop fired
T1 | 10:16:02 |  | Argus Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
T2 | 10:16:04 |  | Argus Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
T3 | 10:16:05 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 10:16
T4 | 10:16:05 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 361 minutes of metrics
T5 | 10:16:05 |  | Investigator Agent Placed the start of the incident at 10:10
T6 | 10:16:05 |  | Investigator Agent Recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
T7 | 10:16:08 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 10:11
T8 | 10:16:08 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 1 production change
T9 | 10:16:08 |  | Investigator Agent Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
T10 | 10:16:08 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 minutes before 10:16
T11 | 10:16:08 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 124 log lines
T12 | 10:16:12 |  | Investigator Agent Formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1
T13 | 10:16:12 |  | Investigator Agent Read every channel available
T14 | 10:16:12 |  | Argus Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 10:16:12
T15 | 10:16:13 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
T16 | 10:16:13 | MITIGATION APPLIED | Mitigation Agent Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
T17 | 10:16:14 |  | Mitigation Agent Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 10:17 - up to 166s
 | 10:17 | IMPACT ENDS | the service was back to normal
T18 | 10:18:09 |  | Mitigation Agent Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 10:16
T19 | 10:18:09 |  | Mitigation Agent Judged the action CONFIRMED
T20 | 10:18:09 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag monthly-spend-feature OFF and the rule that fired stopped firing
T21 | 10:19:03 |  | Code-Fix Agent Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #570

Response effort
none - engineer time
157,792 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/97329cac-20b9-405a-a19d-5608139d88f4
The fix it proposed: PR #570 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/570) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 10:10:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 09:40–10:09
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 36 occurrences in 30 minutes, 09:40–10:09
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 occurrences in 37 minutes, 09:40–10:16; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 10:13
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 occurrences in 26 minutes, 09:41–10:06
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 10:10
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 10:10–10:16
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 10:11–10:16
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py returns account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month), where bought_this_month is the purchases flagged in_current_month. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has an empty list there, so the line raises ZeroDivisionError. That is not an edge case. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py calls it "the ordinary case". With monthly-spend-feature off, render_spend_summary never reached this function. With it on, every such shopper's request reached it, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turned each error into a failed page.

The change: if there are no purchases this month, the function returns 0. Nothing was spent per item this month, and total_this_month_cents is itself 0 for such an account in the fixtures. Otherwise the division is unchanged. With the flag off, nothing changes. average_spend_per_item and the lifetime path are untouched. They still raise for an account that has never bought anything, which the existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py and tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py rely on. render_spend_summary and serve_account_page still get an int, so their return types and callers are unchanged.

The tests: three new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py. Two call the monthly figure directly and through render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) for a shopper with no purchases this month, and expect 0. One expects 0 for a shopper with no history at all when the monthly flag is on. Each of these would raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code. The test that expects a failure to reach the caller on the lifetime path stays as it is.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-11
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, account pages on io-shop failed for shoppers. The failures began when a new monthly spending summary was switched on. Its calculation broke the account page, likely for shoppers who had bought before but had not yet bought this month. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests failed, and Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so no one on call had to respond. Argus ended the incident by switching the new feature off again (reverting the monthly-spend-feature flag), and it is confirmed off and still off. Argus has also proposed a fix in PR #570, but it is still a draft and has not been put in place.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
